root_cause.text: The ksmbd server used memcmp() to compare sensitive cryptographic Message Authentication Codes (MACs), including NTLMv2 hashes and SMB2/SMB3 signatures, which is not constant-time and allows timing side-channel attacks.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states "To prevent timing attacks, MAC comparisons need to be constant-time. Replace the memcmp() with the correct function, crypto_memneq()." The patch replaces memcmp() with crypto_memneq() in three locations: the NTLMv2 hash check in auth.c (`ksmbd_auth_ntlmv2`), and the SMB2 and SMB3 signature checks in smb2pdu.c (`smb2_check_sign_req` and `smb3_check_sign_req`).

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing dependency by selecting CRYPTO_LIB_UTILS when SMB_SERVER is enabled.
intent_record.what: Added a 'select CRYPTO_LIB_UTILS' line under the SMB_SERVER Kconfig entry.
intent_record.how: When SMB_SERVER is enabled, the kernel will now automatically enable CRYPTO_LIB_UTILS, ensuring that required crypto utility functions are available at build and runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Added include for crypto/utils.h to make its utility functions available.
intent_record.what: Added #include <crypto/utils.h> to the list of header includes.
intent_record.how: This enables the compilation unit to use declarations and functions from crypto/utils.h, potentially fixing missing references or enabling new functionality.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace non-constant-time memcmp with constant-time crypto_memneq in NTLMv2 authentication to mitigate timing side-channel attacks.
intent_record.what: Replaced a call to memcmp (with comparison against zero) with a call to crypto_memneq, and adjusted the conditional return to check the return value of crypto_memneq directly.
intent_record.how: The change ensures that the comparison of the NTLMv2 hash is performed in constant time, preventing timing side-channel attacks that could reveal hash values. Authentication behavior remains functionally identical (return -EINVAL on mismatch).

intent_record.intent_summary: Add missing include for crypto utilities header to ensure proper function declarations.
intent_record.what: Added an include directive for <crypto/utils.h> after the copyright comment and before existing includes.
intent_record.how: This change makes the declarations from <crypto/utils.h> available to the source file, preventing potential compilation warnings or errors due to missing function prototypes or type definitions that the code may rely on.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace memcmp with crypto_memneq for constant-time comparison of SMB2 signatures to prevent timing side-channel attacks.
intent_record.what: Replaced memcmp with crypto_memneq in signature comparison inside smb2_check_sign_req.
intent_record.how: The signature comparison now uses a constant-time function (crypto_memneq) instead of memcmp, preventing timing side-channel attacks that could leak the correct signature.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace memcmp with crypto_memneq in SMB3 signature verification to prevent timing side-channel attacks.
intent_record.what: Replaced memcmp with crypto_memneq when comparing SMB2 signatures in smb3_check_sign_req.
intent_record.how: The change makes signature comparison constant-time, preventing timing side-channel attacks that could leak signature comparison results.

relevance_review.reason: The group addresses a missing kernel configuration dependency (CRYPTO_LIB_UTILS) for SMB_SERVER, not the timing side-channel vulnerability caused by using memcmp() for MAC comparison.

The change adds an include for crypto/utils.h, which is necessary to use constant-time comparison functions to replace the vulnerable memcmp() calls. This directly addresses the root cause of the timing side-channel attack.
The group directly replaces non-constant-time memcmp with constant-time crypto_memneq for NTLMv2 authentication, exactly addressing the timing side-channel vulnerability described in the root cause.

The group only adds a missing include for crypto utilities header, which is a compilation fix. It does not directly address the use of non-constant-time memcmp() for cryptographic MAC comparisons, which is the core vulnerability.

The group directly addresses the vulnerability by replacing memcmp with crypto_memneq for constant-time comparison of SMB2 and SMB3 signatures, which are cryptographic MACs vulnerable to timing side-channel attacks.
